question.problem: A cruise ship on the high seas travels at a speed of $972$ centimeters per second. What is the speed of the ship in meters per second?
question.worked_solution:
We are given the units $\frac{\text{cm}}{\text{s}},$ and we want to convert this into $\frac{\text{m}}{\text{s}}.$ To figure out what we need to multiply by, we can set up an equation to help us:

$$
\frac{\text{cm}}{\text{s}}\cdot \,\frac{?}{?}=\frac{\text{m}}{\text{s}}
$$

We want to replace $\text{cm}$ with $\text{m}.$ To get rid of $\text{cm},$ we can put $\text{cm}$ in the denominator so that it cancels out. To introduce $\text{m},$ we can put $\text{m}$ in the numerator.

$$
\frac{\cancel{\text{cm}}}{\text{s}}\cdot \frac{\text{m}}{\cancel{\text{cm}}}=\frac{\text{m}}{\text{s}}
$$

So, our conversion formula is

$$
\frac{\text{cm}}{\text{s}}\cdot \frac{\text{m}}{\text{cm}}=\frac{\text{m}}{\text{s}}.
$$

Now that we have our conversion formula, we need to determine the correct numbers to use, and apply it.

- The speed given in the problem statement is $972\,\frac{\text{cm}}{\text{s}}.$

- There are $100$ centimeters per meter. Taking the reciprocal, there are $\frac{1}{100}$ meters per centimeter.

Applying our conversion formula, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}972\,\frac{\text{cm}}{\text{s}} & =972\,\frac{\text{cm}}{\text{s}}\cdot \frac{1}{100}\,\frac{\text{m}}{\text{cm}} \\  & =972\cdot \frac{1}{100}(\frac{\cancel{\text{cm}}}{\text{s}}\cdot \frac{\text{m}}{\cancel{\text{cm}}}) \\  & =9.72\,\frac{\text{m}}{\text{s}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the speed of the cruise is $9.72\,\text{m}/\text{s}.$
